entries.proposition: 16q23.1 is named as a recurrent pleiotropic region in the abstract.
16q23.1 recurred across all four acute-pancreatitis/fat pairs.
The authors attribute the 16q23.1 locus to CTRB1/CTRB2.
entries.snippet: The 16q23.1 CTRB1/CTRB2 locus regulates trypsinogen and trypsin degradation

entries.proposition: CTRB1 is among genes detected across all four pairs by MAGMA.
entries.snippet: CTRB1, DPYD, PPP1R13B, PRSS1, SPINK1, TM4SF4, TRAF3, and ZFYVE21 were detected across all four pairs

entries.proposition: Gene mapping used GRCh37/hg19 annotation and plus-minus 10 kb windows.
entries.snippet: 1000 Genomes Phase 3 European LD and GENCODE GRCh37/ hg19 annotations

entries.proposition: The authors state window mapping may assign variants to several neighbouring genes.
entries.snippet: may assign variants to multiple neighboring genes, introducing redundancy

entries.proposition: Three loci reached strong colocalization (PP.H4 of at least 0.80); the text does not name them.
entries.snippet: Bayesian colocalization analysis identified three loci with strong shared causal evidence

entries.proposition: Fig. 3 legend: colocalised loci orange, MAGMA genes blue. Rendered panel shows 16q23.1 with BCAR1, CTRB1, CTRB2 labels and no WWOX label; an orange 16q23.1 node on the intrapancreatic-fat branch.
entries.snippet: Colocalized loci are marked in orange, and MAGMA-prioritized genes are shown in blue

entries.proposition: The authors frame results as shared architecture, not causality.
entries.snippet: the findings should be interpreted as shared genetic architecture rather than definitive causality
